name: vertex_bevel_noop_divergence
face_ring_start_note: Measured 2026-08-18, ring by ring: the new corner triangle matches the reference start-and-all, and every RE-RUNG incident face is the reference's ring rotated by exactly one position -- the reference begins the re-rung ring at the first replacement point, we begin it one corner earlier. Same corners, same winding, off by one. So the file's own claim that the corner triangle's "ring order and winding are the reference's exactly" is true of the triangle and NOT of the faces around it, which is the sort of over-read a rotation-tolerant green invites. Nothing here is re-measured: the fix is a one-position shift in our vertex-bevel re-ringing, filed in doc/tasks/backlog/1311-ring-start-laws-to-capture.md, and this stays rotation-tolerant until it lands.
description: CLOSED BY IMPLEMENTATION (task 1240, ledger rows 26/52). This file was frozen as a CAPABILITY GAP: the reference chamfered a vertex and we did nothing at all -- our command answered `did not apply` and the mesh came back byte-identical to its input, in 46 of the 57 vertex-bevel cells of the sweep, and in 181 of 181 cells of the ring-rotation sweep. The kernel required an INTERIOR-MANIFOLD vertex of valence >= 3, so a boundary corner -- including the smallest case there is, one corner of one quad -- was declined outright. The rule the frozen numbers state was implemented as stated: each edge at the chamfered vertex contributes a point at `inset` along it measured from the vertex, the vertex itself is removed, every incident face is re-rung through those points, and at valence >= 3 a new face closes the corner (at valence 2 there is none -- a two-point polygon is not what the reference emits). Both cases now declare an EMPTY gap in the vertex AND the face channel, which the same runner checks just as strictly as a full one: our counts, our vertex set and our face rings WITH WINDING equal the reference's. The cases are kept, not deleted -- the reference measurement is the valuable half and it is unchanged.
source: Reference side: headless command-port capture of the vertex-bevel tool at inset 0.12 (dirty-geometry sweep, task 1123, cases vbev_pole_np_one / vbev_pole_triquad). vibe3d side: live drive of this build -- the command is rejected, which the fixture records with allowError.

provenance.notes: INSTRUMENT: the reference side is a BEHAVIOURAL CAPTURE driven through the reference editor's own headless command port -- no display, no pointer, no debugger and no static read of its binary; every number in `reference` is a coordinate the reference itself printed after running the operation on the mesh in `input`. The vibe3d side is a LIVE DRIVE of this build over the HTTP test API through the very steps this fixture stores, read back from /api/model. Both engines are given the SAME base mesh (the reference's own dump, injected verbatim) and the selection travels by COORDINATE, so no element index is assumed to mean the same thing on both sides. Nothing here is an inference about the reference's internals; where a MECHANISM is guessed at, the case note says so in that word.

cases.name: boundary_corner_of_folded_quad
cases.note: Valence-2 boundary corner (0,0,0) of a folded quad, inset 0.12. Both engines: 5 vertices, 5 edges, one PENTAGON -- the corner is replaced by (0.12,0,0) and (0,0.01194,0.119404), and NO cap face is emitted at valence 2. This is the smallest case in the family and the one the old interior-manifold guard rejected most bluntly. EMPTY GAP since task 1240.

cases.name: valence_three_corner
cases.note: Valence-3 corner (1,0,0) of a quad+triangle base, inset 0.12 -- a BOUNDARY vertex (two of its three edges carry one face each), which is why valence alone never explained the old refusal. Both engines: 7 vertices, 9 edges, 3 faces -- the corner becomes (0.88,0,0), (1,0,0.12) and (1.107331,0,0.053666), each 0.12 along one of its three edges, with a new triangle closing the corner. That triangle's ring order and winding are the reference's exactly, not merely its vertex set. EMPTY GAP since task 1240.
